Notre Dame Fighting Irish.career_experience: Established starter; spent spring and summer as Heisman favorite.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.rushing: Three rushing scores; the guide notes he is not the running threat Riley Leonard was.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.turnovers: Six interceptions against 24 touchdown passes. The guide flags a team-level caution — Notre Dame is +31 in turnover margin over two seasons, an area of concern unless Carr protects the ball.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.competition: None described — Carr is the settled starter.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.backup: Not addressed by name; the guide calls the depth behind him a major worry if anything happens.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.author_confidence: High. Asked whether there are any weaknesses on offense, the guide's answer is no.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.positive_case: A 24-to-6 ratio, a very good offensive line with Charles Jagusah back, and a schedule the guide says should produce numbers for a very visible programme.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.concerns: Two, both stated plainly: he is not the running threat Riley Leonard was, and the depth behind him is a major worry if anything happens. The guide also attributes his Heisman favoritism substantially to the schedule.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.supporting_cast: Strong despite losses. Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price take over 2,000 rushing yards and 29 scores with them, but Aneyas Williams should keep the standard; Jordan Faison is the only notable returning receiver though Jaden Greathouse returns from injury; and the line looks very good with Charles Jagusah back.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.portal_context: The guide offers a culture signal as evidence: the Irish were so aggrieved by the playoff snub that they skipped a bowl, and the only notable departures went to the NFL rather than to other schools.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 11.5 wins, with the guide naming the risk honestly: the pressure of going perfect may prove too much. Miami is treated as the only major stumbling block. Projection is 11.42 wins, with Notre Dame favored by 8.5 or more in every game.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.outlook_dependency: Moderate on performance, high on availability. The guide finds no weakness in Carr's play, but names quarterback depth as a major worry and ties turnover regression to his ball security.

Rice Owls.status: Transfer — via UCF, having previously been at Miami.
Rice Owls.career_experience: Two years each at Miami and UCF.
Rice Owls.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Rice Owls.passing: Only 148 career passes, with more interceptions than touchdowns — nine to six.
Rice Owls.rushing: 137 carries for 821 yards, better than six per carry.
Rice Owls.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate.
Rice Owls.turnovers: Nine interceptions against six touchdown passes across 148 attempts.
Rice Owls.competition: None described — Brown is presented as the starter.
Rice Owls.author_confidence: Qualified. The guide allows Brown could be a difference-maker as a better runner than Chase Jenkins, while doubting the scheme's viability in this conference.
Rice Owls.positive_case: A genuine runner at better than six yards per carry, and a better runner than his predecessor.
Rice Owls.concerns: A negative touchdown-to-interception ratio on a small passing sample, in an offense the guide expects to throw even less.
Rice Owls.scheme_fit: Central and quantified. The guide supplies the schematic precedent from Scott Abell's Davidson, where quarterbacks attempted only 152 passes in 11 games while the team ran 640 times for 3,720 yards, with quarterback Andrew Frazier third in both rushing attempts and yards. With Rice at 647 rushing attempts against 224 passes last season, it expects an even starker split.
Rice Owls.supporting_cast: Thin. Quinton Jackson was Rice's best offensive player with 889 yards at 4.9 per carry.
Rice Owls.portal_context: Abell brought in a decent number of Power Four transfers, Brown among them.
Rice Owls.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 3.5 wins. The schedule is the crux: favorable last season, not now — Rice faces all the teams projected average or better apart from Navy and does not play Charlotte or UAB, its only two conference wins. The guide flags the finale specifically: if Rice is 3-8 going in, which it calls plausible, the last game is against Army, a terrible matchup for a less accomplished option team. Projection is 3.72 wins.
Rice Owls.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's scheme argument runs through the quarterback, while its conclusion is that this may not be the best conference for the approach regardless of who plays.

South Florida Bulls.status: Transfer — arriving via LSU, having previously been at Mississippi State; replacing Byrum Brown, who left with Alex Golesh.
South Florida Bulls.career_experience: Four starts and relief work at LSU last season.
South Florida Bulls.passing: An 8-to-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio at LSU across four starts and relief work.
South Florida Bulls.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate.
South Florida Bulls.turnovers: Two interceptions against eight touchdown passes at LSU.
South Florida Bulls.competition: Not described as settled. The guide notes Hartline and coordinator Tim Beck added both Van Buren and Luke Kromenhoek, via Florida State and Mississippi State.
South Florida Bulls.backup: Luke Kromenhoek, via Florida State and Mississippi State.
South Florida Bulls.author_confidence: Positive on the individual, uncertain about the whole. The guide credits Van Buren with genuine success while framing the roster as highly touted recruits dropping down to get back on the radar.
South Florida Bulls.positive_case: An 8-to-2 ratio at LSU, and a roster philosophy the guide explains rather than dismisses: the portal lets highly touted recruits who did not make it drop to a Group of Six programme to get back on the radar, and at South Florida most such players are quarterbacks.
South Florida Bulls.concerns: He replaces enormous production — South Florida was one of five teams averaging 40-plus points, and 49 in American play, with Byrum Brown producing over 4,000 yards and 42 touchdowns — and most of the surrounding portal acquisitions did not play much previously.
South Florida Bulls.scheme_fit: The guide states its reservation about coordinator Tim Beck openly: it took him 35 years to get a head job, Coastal Carolina did not go well at 20-18, and it personally finds him underwhelming as a coordinator.
South Florida Bulls.supporting_cast: Almost entirely new. The guide notes most portal acquisitions did not play much previously, then supplies the counterweight: 247Sports graded South Florida's portal haul the best in the conference and 58th nationally with 44 commits.
South Florida Bulls.portal_context: 44 portal commits, graded best in the conference and 58th nationally by 247Sports; Van Buren and Kromenhoek are the quarterback additions.
South Florida Bulls.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins, with a basically new roster and a first-time head coach. The guide makes a sharp market observation: South Florida could be favored in 10 or 11 games, yet the vig slants toward the Under, reflecting how many unanswered questions have the market down on the programme. Projection is 8.56 wins.
South Florida Bulls.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide's first stated task for Hartline is sustaining Golesh's offensive standards after losing the quarterback who produced them.

Temple Owls.status: New starter, identity undetermined — Evan Simon and backup Gevani McCoy are gone and the guide says there is virtually no experience.
Temple Owls.previous_school: Jaxon Smolik comes from Penn State; Ajani Sheppard from Rutgers, having also been at Washington State.
Temple Owls.career_experience: Jaxon Smolik played four games in three years at Penn State; Ajani Sheppard played five games at Rutgers and none at Washington State.
Temple Owls.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as counts.
Temple Owls.passing: Not addressed in guide for either candidate.
Temple Owls.turnovers: Not addressed in guide for either candidate. The departing starter Evan Simon posted a 25-to-2 ratio and led Temple to its first positive turnover margin in some time, against -10, -20 and -11 under Stan Drayton.
Temple Owls.competition: Open between two inexperienced transfers, Jaxon Smolik and Ajani Sheppard, with the guide naming no favourite.
Temple Owls.backup: The two named candidates are Jaxon Smolik and Ajani Sheppard.
Temple Owls.author_confidence: Very low. The guide's conclusion is that a huge downturn looks likely.
Temple Owls.positive_case: Not addressed in guide for either candidate.
Temple Owls.concerns: Virtually no experience, replacing a quarterback whose specific value the guide characterizes precisely: safe, reliable throws that did not generate much yardage — only 19 touchdown passes after six in the opener against UMass — but which protected the ball and gave an undermanned defense a better chance.
Temple Owls.scheme_fit: Not addressed in guide for the new candidates; under K.C. Keeler and former Montana State coordinator Tyler Walker the offense improved by more than a touchdown per game last season.
Temple Owls.supporting_cast: Not addressed in guide in detail; the guide notes more returnees on offense than defense.
Temple Owls.portal_context: Smolik from Penn State and Sheppard from Rutgers are the named additions.
Temple Owls.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, with the guide asking directly where the wins come from. Its decisive argument is that Keeler could not reach six wins with a +11 turnover margin last season, and this group looks worse at the most important position. Projection is 5.33 wins.
Temple Owls.outlook_dependency: Very high. The quarterback downgrade is the guide's decisive stated argument for the Under.
Temple Owls.conflicts: The guide names two candidates and declines to state an expected starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Tulane Green Wave.status: New starter, identity undetermined — the guide names two candidates and answers its own question with “we do not know”.
Tulane Green Wave.previous_school: Kadin Semonza started at Ball State; Zeon Chriss-Gremillion's previous schools are not addressed.
Tulane Green Wave.career_experience: Zeon Chriss-Gremillion has played a very long time in college; Kadin Semonza redshirted without playing after starting at Ball State.
Tulane Green Wave.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as counts.
Tulane Green Wave.competition: Open between Zeon Chriss-Gremillion and Kadin Semonza, with the guide dryly noting that the most notable development about the former is his hyphenated name.
Tulane Green Wave.backup: The two named candidates are Zeon Chriss-Gremillion and Kadin Semonza.
Tulane Green Wave.author_confidence: Explicitly none. Asked who the impact players on offense are, the guide's answer is simply that we do not know.
Tulane Green Wave.concerns: The guide observes that neither Darian Mensah, Jake Retzlaff nor all-time passing leader Michael Pratt is walking through the door, and raises a counterfactual: had Retzlaff not violated BYU's Honor Code, Tulane may have been great enough to be the Group of Five playoff representative.
Tulane Green Wave.supporting_cast: Weak. The guide argues Retzlaff's availability was a gift because Tulane was poorly set at running back after Makhi Hughes transferred: Jamauri McClure averaged 6.5 yards per carry on 83 attempts while Javin Gordon managed 4.0 on 128. Leading receiver Shazz Preston is gone, leaving Anthony Brown-Stevenson, who had only two fewer catches.
Tulane Green Wave.portal_context: Tulane's portal class ranks seventh among 14 American teams, which the guide calls unimpressive for a programme with three 11-win seasons and a 9-5 campaign in four years.
Tulane Green Wave.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, with the guide explicitly noting the tension — and yet the schedule should help in a big way. It also revises its own view of the coach openly: Will Hall has had two stints at Tulane and success at West Alabama and West Georgia, so he may deserve more benefit of the doubt than his messy Southern Miss tenure had earned him. Projection is 7.56 wins.
Tulane Green Wave.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide's regression case offers Retzlaff — who led the team in rushing with 16 rushing scores — as one of three candidate explanations for last season's record, and it does not know who replaces him.
Tulane Green Wave.conflicts: The guide names two candidates and declines to state an expected starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Tulsa Golden Hurricane.status: Returning starter — the guide highlights that he did not leave when most of the roster did.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.career_experience: Freshman starter in 2025 heading into a sophomore season.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.passing: Not addressed in guide as a season line; the guide says he did not post eye-popping numbers but led the offense to 424 yards in the upset of Oklahoma State.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide expects more designed runs for him.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.turnovers: Not addressed in guide individually; team-level, Tulsa managed 11 takeaways for a -9 turnover margin.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.competition: None described — Hayes is the settled starter.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.author_confidence: Positive on retention rather than production. The guide says his staying could make a major difference despite an entirely new skill group.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.positive_case: He led the offense to 424 yards in the upset of Oklahoma State that changed perceptions of the programme's direction, and the guide makes a structural point: with the programme showing more stability, transfers are now more willing to come.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.concerns: He loses 1,000-yard rusher Dominic Richardson and his top three pass catchers, and the guide is careful to give the full sequence around the Oklahoma State upset — Tulsa followed with three straight blowout losses to conference top dogs, then was largely competitive against comparable or lesser opponents.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.scheme_fit: New coordinator Kevin Barbay arrives, and the open question the guide poses is whether he and head coach Tre Lamb can inject life into the offense.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.supporting_cast: Rebuilt, with the line the strength. The guide jokes Tulsa should get a steak NIL deal given the beef up front: Lamb brought transfers from Texas A&M and Ole Miss last season and added South Alabama's starting center Malachi Preciado, originally at Purdue, with every starter and two-deep player at or above 300 pounds. It expects heavy running with productive Auburn and Old Dominion transfers at running back, and with nearly 500 rushing attempts last season it expects an even higher figure.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.portal_context: Running back transfers from Auburn and Old Dominion, plus Malachi Preciado at center from South Alabama.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 5.5 wins, framed as giving Lamb and his staff the benefit of the doubt despite a challenging schedule. Tulsa avoids East Carolina and Memphis but travels to Navy, Tulane and UTSA. The guide identifies the hinge: beating Sam Houston State on the road in Week 2 should get this home and produce a first bowl since 2021. Projection is 5.43 wins.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.outlook_dependency: High. The guide names quarterback continuity as the thing that could make a major difference in a year of otherwise total turnover.

UAB Blazers.status: Transfer — arriving via West Virginia, having previously been at BYU.
UAB Blazers.competition: None described — Burton is presented as at least a starting point.
UAB Blazers.author_confidence: Minimal, and phrased as such: the guide calls Burton at least a starting point, and states that nobody on the two-deep is proven.
UAB Blazers.positive_case: The guide offers only that he is a starting point.
UAB Blazers.concerns: It is frank that many offensive players are multi-time transfers who have not latched on anywhere, including a patchwork line, and that UAB returns one player with more than 20 tackles.
UAB Blazers.scheme_fit: Trent Dilfer's successor Alex Mortensen was coordinator when promoted, kept calling plays as interim and will continue while overseeing the whole programme; the guide finds a mitigating factor in veteran defensive coordinator Todd Grantham, who does not need supervision.
UAB Blazers.supporting_cast: Almost entirely new and unproven, with a patchwork offensive line. Georgia transfer Rod Robinson and ULM transfer Bam McReynolds are named as focal points, since the guide notes little changed for the offense late last season beyond running more often.
UAB Blazers.portal_context: Portal additions from all over make up the defense and most of the offense; the guide is frank that many are multi-time transfers who have not latched on anywhere.
UAB Blazers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 3.5 wins. The guide acknowledges UAB reached four wins amid turmoil while calling the schedule pretty rough, and reasons through specific games: ULM should be a win but comes second with many new players and schemes, making it high-variance either way. A game-state argument closes it: because the guide expects the pass game to become less important, it worries UAB projects to trail often. Projection is 3.63 wins.
UAB Blazers.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Under rests on wholesale roster turnover and schedule rather than on quarterback play specifically.

UTSA Roadrunners.career_experience: The programme's third-leading passer, who will pass Eric Soza for second in Week 1 against UTRGV but will not catch Frank Harris, whose job he took over fully in 2024.
UTSA Roadrunners.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide records he took the job over fully in 2024.
UTSA Roadrunners.passing: Fell just short of 3,000 passing yards with 30 touchdown passes.
UTSA Roadrunners.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate.
UTSA Roadrunners.competition: None described — McCown is the settled starter.
UTSA Roadrunners.author_confidence: High. The guide ties UTSA's ceiling to McCown and asks directly whether he will be the best quarterback in the conference.
UTSA Roadrunners.positive_case: Nearly 3,000 yards with 30 touchdown passes, rapport with returning receivers, and a coordinator the guide expects to unlock more.
UTSA Roadrunners.concerns: Top receiver Devin McCuin was taken by Ohio State — and the guide notes drily that they know something about receivers.
UTSA Roadrunners.scheme_fit: Rated an interesting hire: Rick Bowie arrives after Western Kentucky last season, Abilene Christian in 2024 and Valdosta State in 2022-23, having led prolific passing offenses, and the guide calls him a very intriguing fit for one of the American's most experienced offenses.
UTSA Roadrunners.supporting_cast: Solid. McCown has rapport with David Amador and AJ Wilson plus longer-tenured players, on one of the American's most experienced offenses.
UTSA Roadrunners.portal_context: Per 247Sports UTSA brought in 21 transfers, 12 on defense, though its class ranks 11th of the 12 American teams with portal access; a good chunk of money was earmarked to improve the roster.
UTSA Roadrunners.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins. UTSA has lost to Army in all three American seasons but avoids them this year, while drawing Navy at home along with South Florida and an improved Tulsa; the toughest conference test is a late-October trip to Tulane. The guide's conclusion is that Jeff Traylor must avoid bad losses but this may well be the best team in the conference. Projection is 7.77 wins.
UTSA Roadrunners.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide states directly that UTSA's ceiling is tied to McCown.
